title: Design System: Outside In Bass Lab

rack.purpose: Behind everything; the gap between units.

face.purpose: A faceplate. The working surface of a screen.

face-2.purpose: A module raised off the plate: head and transport.

well.purpose: Milled out. Readouts, neck, tab, tables, fields.

bone.purpose: Silkscreen. Four steps of printing hierarchy.

oxide.purpose: The next move. One per screen, or none.

signal.purpose: Amplifier green. Present, correct, in key, passed.

alert.purpose: Missed, avoid, outside, out of tolerance.

olive.purpose: Tertiary marks and meter minor ticks.

display.purpose: The one statement at the top of a screen. Barlow Condensed 700.

title.purpose: Section headings, written as statements rather than labels.

body.purpose: Barlow, capped at a 38rem measure inside any workspace width.

label.purpose: Nomenclature above a control. Never above a heading.

readout.purpose: Azeret Mono, tabular. Every quantity on the instrument.

shadows.name: depth-panel
shadows.purpose: A faceplate: lit on top, shadowed under. Bolted, not floating.

shadows.name: depth-well
shadows.purpose: Milled out. Readouts, fields, tables, the neck.

shadows.name: depth-press
shadows.purpose: A switch pressed in; the light moves to the bottom lip.

shadows.name: depth-chassis
shadows.purpose: The only outer shadow: where the transport meets the plate.

shadows.name: bezel
shadows.purpose: The ring a seated lamp or screw sits in.

shadows.name: lamp-lit
shadows.purpose: A tight bleed onto the paint. Never a bloom.

motion.name: m-click
motion.purpose: Switch throw, key press, lamp on.

motion.name: m-sweep
motion.purpose: Needle travel, progression change, note reseat.

motion.name: ease-mech
motion.purpose: Mechanical settle. Fast off the mark, no overshoot: a detent, not a spring.

components.name: Lamp Row
components.description: Indicator lamps. An unlit lamp is still visibly a lamp, because a panel with none and a panel with one dark are different objects.

components.name: Well Readout
components.description: A quantity milled into the plate. Tabular so a changing number never shifts its neighbours.

components.name: Engraved Section
components.description: The system signature: one plate, sections divided by a routed groove. Not a card, and no kicker above the heading.

narrative.overview: This is a piece of equipment, not a page about one. Warm charcoal faceplates under tungsten, aged bone nomenclature silkscreened onto them, wells milled out where a quantity has to be read, and lamps that are either lit or not. A screen is a single faceplate with its sections engraved into it, not a stack of tiles. Depth comes from one inversion: a panel catches light on its top edge, a well catches it on the bottom lip, and that difference carries every relationship in the interface. Colour is a signal path. Green reports present and correct, oxide says this is the next move, red says a miss.
keyCharacteristics: One faceplate per screen, divided by engraved grooves rather than by gaps.
Two depths only: bolted panel, milled well. Nothing floats.
Colour is a lamp. Green correct, oxide next, red missed.
Square corners at 2px, the radius a router bit actually leaves.
Condensed nomenclature, upright prose, mono for every measurement.
Hardware time: nothing moves for longer than 300ms.

rules.name: The One Oxide Rule
rules.body: A screen has one oxide element, and none when there is no next action. Two oxide elements means one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Lamp Rule
rules.body: Colour reports state. If an element is not telling the player something true right now, it is bone or unpainted.

rules.name: The Warm Ground Rule
rules.body: Every neutral carries the olive-brown cast. A cool grey or blue-black reads as a screen instead of painted steel.

rules.name: The Legend Rule
rules.body: A legend names a control or a readout. It never sits above a section heading. Kickers are banned outright.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every quantity is mono with tabular figures. A tempo that shifts its neighbours going from 99 to 100 is a broken instrument.

rules.name: The One Plate Rule
rules.body: A screen is one faceplate with grooves cut across it. Sections are separated by a routed line, never by a gap between boxes.

rules.name: The Transport Never Hides
rules.body: The strip may drop labels as width shrinks, but never a function. A player mid-take cannot go looking for stop.

rules.name: The Two Depths Rule
rules.body: Bolted or milled. A third elevation, a floating card, or a resting drop shadow does not exist in this system.

rules.name: The Milled Corner Rule
rules.body: 2px everywhere, 3px in a well. A pill or a 12px card radius belongs to a different object.

dos: Do treat a screen as one faceplate with grooves cut across it.
Do keep one oxide control per screen, and none when there is no next action.
Do mill a well for anything that reports a quantity, and only for that.
Do set every number in Azeret Mono with tabular figures.
Do put a legend above a control and nowhere else.
Do keep motion between 120ms and 300ms, on transform and opacity.
Do self-host any new face as WOFF2 under /fonts with its licence.
Do clear 44px on every target under a coarse pointer.
Do collapse all motion to 1ms under prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't give a section its own background, border and padding. That is the card layout in costume.
Don't add a resting drop shadow, a third elevation, or a radius above 3px.
Don't put a kicker above a heading. This one has no exception.
Don't use a text arrow as an icon. Transport and caret glyphs are drawn.
Don't colour anything that is not reporting state.
Don't introduce a cool grey or a blue-black; every neutral is warm.
Don't use a bounce or elastic easing. Mechanisms have detents, not springs.
Don't link a font, script or stylesheet from a third-party CDN.
Don't hide a transport function to save width. Drop the label instead.
Don't number a section in its heading, or use an em-dash in visible text.
